messages:
incident-bot: ALERT • canary-route-slo • region=eu-central • fired at 03:12 UTC — p95 latency > 700ms for 10m
dan: saw the page, joining
deploy-bot: deploy v2.18 started 01:40 UTC — traffic split script applied at 02:58 UTC
natalie: who owns the traffic-split script?
rui: that was me — small change to selector logic to include `route=canary` and `route=canary-shadow` to ease shadowing tests
jess: why are both labeled the same? that seems risky
rui: intended to share lb path but separate backend, guess the templating collapsed them into identical labels
calvin-support: we have 5 customer tickets about slow responses referencing inference endpoints  /v1/generate — customers: C-113, C-114, C-115, C-118, C-119
ops-bot: top-level check: canary pods OK, replicas 3/3, readiness passing
dan: metrics show p95 high for `http_request_duration_seconds` but only when filtered by label `route="canary"`. suspiciously, the canary-shadow series has same label so queries double-count
jess: that could explain an SLO "burn" — alert rule sums by route label and treats both series as one
calvin-support: customers report degraded latency starting ~03:00 UTC
deploy-bot: rollback-procedure available: `rw deploy rollback --service=ingress --to=v2.17`
natalie: before rolling back, can we mute alerts and confirm customer impact scope? we should coordinate comms
oncall-pager: paging #eng-oncall -> dan, natalie, rui
support-bot: initial customer messages sent: template ack + troubleshooting notice (ETA 30m)
rui: temporary mitigation: flip traffic-split to exclude canary-shadow and isolate canary. running:
```
# update traffic-split real quick
scripts/traffic-split --service ingress --remove-label route=canary-shadow --env prod --dry-run=false
```

rui: applied, waiting on LB convergence
jess: can we mute the noisy SLO alert for the region while we validate?
oncall-pager: muting alert group `canary-route-slo` for 20m (muted by natalie)

natalie: confirmed LB logs: requests to canary-shadow are being routed to the same backend pool due to identical label values — doubling load on canary pool
dan: scaling canary down is fastest mitigation. scaling to 1 replica to drain traffic from overloaded pods

# command
kubectl -n inference scale deploy/redwood-canary-ingress --replicas=1

natalie: scaling done, observing p95 trending down at edge
calvin-support: updating customers: "We've isolated the experimental shadow routing and reduced traffic to affected canary pods. Performance should improve; monitoring now."
rui: root cause: traffic-split templating introduced label collision between canary and shadow lanes during the v2.18 rollout packaging. Additionally, the alert rule aggregated by `route` expected unique labels; collision caused overcounting and an apparent SLO burn. Missing: a post-deploy smokecheck that verifies uniqueness of route labels in metrics
jess: follow-ups: add a lint to traffic-split templating, add a rule to CI smokechecks that queries Prometheus for distinct label values after deploy, and ensure alerts alert on explicit job+instance when available rather than a single label
dan: opening rollback PR is optional — we fixed routing at infra level; but we should still roll back the templating change in traffic-split package and re-deploy with tests
rui: PR opened: infra#901 traffic-split-template-fix
jess: alerts PR: alerts#421 add aggregate sanity check + mute window automation
natalie: handing off to dan for post-incident follow-up and blameless writeup. Dan will own customer follow-ups and the RCA doc
oncall-pager: handoff acknowledged — next oncall: dan until 10:00 UTC
dan: follow-ups I'm recording:
- add CI smokecheck that runs `prometheus/api/v1/query?query=count(count_values("route", http_request_duration_seconds))` to surface duplicate label values
- add unit test for templating to prevent collapsed label assignments
- create runbook step: after traffic-split changes, verify LB mapping and prometheus label cardinality within 5m
- consider changing alert: from sum by(route) to sum by(job,instance,route) where possible to reduce label-collision risk
calvin-support: will send closure update to customers after RCA is drafted
deploy-bot: ALERT RESOLVED • canary-route-slo • auto-ack after mitigation
natalie: quick summary for incident channel: during v2.18 rollout a templating change caused route label collision between canary and canary-shadow lanes; alerts aggregated collided series and produced an SLO burn; mitigation: isolate canary-shadow, scale canary down, mute alert, crate PRs for fix; limited customer impact and customers notified
dan: linking incident doc & timeline in internal tracker: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1887654321
oncall-pager: closing page — re-escalate with `@oncall` if any regression
support-bot: final customers informed; tickets updated and will be closed once RCA published
jess: putting a short TODO in alerts runbook: "after deploy, verify alert queries return expected series counts"
natalie: thanks everyone — good catch and quick mitigation :thumbsup:

-- end of thread --
